                [32m'The CLI proves correctness of shared memory by allowing one user to read back content that was added by the other user.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Implement a Node.js TypeScript CLI under `/home/user/myproject` that:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Uses the official `@alchemystai/sdk` package.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Authenticates with `ALCHEMYST_AI_API_KEY` from the environment.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Derives a shared `sessionId` from `/logs/artifacts/run-id`, namespaced so it cannot collide with other parallel runs.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Accepts a required `--user-id <id>` flag (used as the Alchemyst memory `userId`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Accepts exactly one of the following operation flags per invocation:\n'[39m +
                [32m'    * `--add "<content>"` — store a new memory under the given `userId` and the shared `sessionId` using `client.v1.context.memory.add(...)`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'    * `--query "<query>"` — search shared memory using `client.v1.context.memory.search(...)` with the given `userId` and the shared `sessionId`, and print every recovered memory.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * If `--user-id` is missing, the CLI must fail with a non-zero exit code and emit a message that includes the string `MISSING_PARAMETERS` (the same error code Alchemyst returns when `userId` or `sessionId` are absent) so the caller knows both `userId` and `sessionId` are mandatory for memory operations.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * On `--add` success, print a single confirmation line of the form `ADDED: <content>` to stdout.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * On `--query`, print every memory returned by Alchemyst, one per line, in the exact format `MEMORY: <content>`. The CLI must surface the contents of all memories that the SDK returns (including those that were added by a different `userId` in the same session).\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * Configure search with a low/lenient similarity threshold so semantically related entries are reliably retrieved.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Provide a complete, build-able project:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `package.json` with a `build` script that produces a runnable bundle/entry at `dist/main.js`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `tsconfig.json` configured to emit JavaScript that Node.js v24 can execute directly via `node dist/main.js ...`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * All dependencies declared in `package.json` (no global installs).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* The TypeScript SDK exposes memory operations under `client.v1.context.memory.add({ userId, sessionId, content })` and `client.v1.context.memory.search({ userId, sessionId, ... })`. See the https://getalchemystai.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart-memory and the https://getalchemystai.com/docs/tutorials/typescript-agent.md.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Both `userId` and `sessionId` are mandatory; omitting either yields `MISSING_PARAMETERS` from the API. Validate `--user-id` locally before calling the SDK so the CLI fails fast with the same error code surface.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* To avoid cross-run collisions when multiple evaluations run in parallel, build the shared `sessionId` as something like `team-standup-<run-id>` (read `/logs/artifacts/run-id` from `process.env`). All invocations within a single run must use the same derived `sessionId`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Memory entries added by different `userId` values that share the same `sessionId` form one common thread; either user can recall the other's contributions via search.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Use a permissive `similarity_threshold` / `minimum_similarity_threshold` (e.g. around `0.1`–`0.3`) so semantically loose queries still retrieve the stored entries.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Iterate over the returned `memories` array and print each entry's textual content prefixed with `MEMORY: ` on its own line so it is trivially greppable.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Do not hardcode `userId`, `sessionId`, or memory content — they all come from CLI args / environment variables.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Use any standard CLI argument parser of your choice (or a manual `process.argv` walk).'[39m
            }
          ]
        },

            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +

            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.).             [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose\n'[39m +

            [32m'   Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands\n'[39m +
            [32m'- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:\n'[39m +
            [32m'<example>\n'[39m +
            [32m`git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'\n`[39m +
            [32m'Commit message here.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'🤖 Generated with [Pochi](https://getpochi.com) | [Task](<Share URL>)\n'[39m +

            [32m'Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
